cards.explanation: The answer is True, friends. "In vain" means the plotting goes nowhere. You can see it in what comes next: God laughs, and then He announces He has already installed His King on Zion (Psalm 2:4, 6). Plan after plan, and not one of them gets off the counter.

The answer is the LORD and His Anointed One, friends. The psalm says the kings take their stand "…against the LORD and against His Anointed One…" (Psalm 2:2). That's the whole target of the meeting. It's a big crowd of rulers all aimed in one direction, and it's the wrong direction.

The answer is break them and cast them away, bakers. The kings say, "Let us break Their chains and cast away Their cords" (Psalm 2:3). Breaking them and casting them away is exactly what they say they want.

The answer is laughs, friends. "The One enthroned in heaven laughs; the Lord taunts them" (Psalm 2:4). All that plotting down on earth, and up in heaven He laughs. I still think about that every time I plan something big.

The answer is False, bakers. After the laugh comes a rebuke: "Then He rebukes them in His anger, and terrifies them in His fury…" (Psalm 2:5). Then He says, "I have installed My King on Zion…" (Psalm 2:6). So the laugh isn't the last word.

The answer is that He has installed His King on Zion, friends. He says, "I have installed My King on Zion, upon My holy mountain" (Psalm 2:6). Notice the word "have." God announces it as something He has already done.

The answer is that He is close to the LORD like a son, bakers. The LORD says, "You are My Son; today I have become Your Father" (Psalm 2:7). That's a father-and-son kind of closeness. And it's the same King He installed on Zion.

The answer is True, friends. The LORD says, "Ask Me, and I will make the nations Your inheritance, the ends of the earth Your possession" (Psalm 2:8). It's a big gift, and it starts with a simple request. I can't think of a better deal on any counter.

The answer is an iron scepter, bakers. "You will break them with an iron scepter; You will shatter them like pottery" (Psalm 2:9). A scepter is a king's rod, and iron is a strong metal. Pottery doesn't stand a chance against that.

The answer is serve the LORD with fear, friends. The psalm says, "Serve the LORD with fear, and rejoice with trembling" (Psalm 2:11). After telling the kings to be wise, it tells them whom to serve. Kings who showed up to break chains are now told to serve.

The answer is rebellion, bakers. The warning says the kings could "…perish in your rebellion…" (Psalm 2:12). Rebellion is exactly what they came to do back in verse 3. The psalm calls it what it is, and then it offers them a way out.
The answer is False, friends. The psalm says "…when His wrath ignites in an instant" (Psalm 2:12). That's the opposite of slow. It's the reason the kings are told to act wisely now.

The answer is all who take refuge in Him, bakers. The psalm ends, "Blessed are all who take refuge in Him" (Psalm 2:12). After all that warning, the last line is good news, and it's for all who take refuge. I love a psalm that finishes warm.
